13	
14	class VariantRail:
15	    def __init__(self, database: str):
16	        self.store = Store(database)
17	
18	    def _idempotent(self, key: str | None, operation: str, action: Callable[[], dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
19	        if not key:
20	            raise ValidationError("Idempotency-Key header is required")
21	        with self.store.transaction() as connection:
22	            existing = connection.execute("SELECT operation, response FROM idempotency WHERE key = ?", (key,)).fetchone()
23	            if existing:
24	                if existing["operation"] != operation:
25	                    raise ConflictError("idempotency key was already used for another operation")
26	                return self.store.decode(existing["response"])
27	            response = action()
28	            connection.execute(
29	                "INSERT INTO idempotency(key, operation, response) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
30	                (key, operation, self.store.encode(response)),
31	            )
32	            return response
33	
34	    def create_sample(self, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
35	        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != {"id", "vcf"}:
36	            raise ValidationError("sample must contain exactly id and vcf")
37	        sample_id = identifier(raw["id"], "sample id")
38	        vcf_text = raw["vcf"]
39	        if not isinstance(vcf_text, str):
40	            raise ValidationError("vcf must be a string")
41	        parsed = parse_vcf(vcf_text)
42	        document = {
43	            "chromosomes": parsed["chromosomes"],
44	            "id": sample_id,
45	            "meta": parsed["meta"],
46	            "records": parsed["records"],
47	            "sha256": digest_text(vcf_text),
48	            "vcf": vcf_text,
49	        }
50	
51	        def create() -> dict[str, Any]:
52	            try:
53	                self.store.connection.execute(
54	                    "INSERT INTO samples(id, document) VALUES (?, ?)",
55	                    (sample_id, self.store.encode(document)),
56	                )
57	            except Exception as error:
58	                if "UNIQUE constraint" in str(error):
59	                    raise ConflictError(f"sample {sample_id} already exists") from error
60	                raise
61	            return sample_view(document)
62	
63	        return self._idempotent(key, f"create-sample:{sample_id}", create)
64	
65	    def get_sample(self, sample_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
66	        row = self.store.connection.execute("SELECT document FROM samples WHERE id = ?", (sample_id,)).fetchone()
67	        if not row:
68	            raise NotFoundError(f"sample {sample_id} was not found")
69	        return self.store.decode(row["document"])
70	
71	    def create_run(self, sample_id: str, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
72	        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or "id" not in raw or set(raw) - {"id", "params"}:
73	            raise ValidationError("run must contain exactly id and optional params")
74	        run_id = identifier(raw["id"], "run id")
75	        params = normalize_params(raw.get("params"))
76	
77	        def create() -> dict[str, Any]:
78	            sample = self.get_sample(sample_id)
79	            result = execute({"records": sample["records"]}, sample["vcf"], params)
80	            document = {
81	                "id": run_id,
82	                "params": params,
83	                "provenance": result["provenance"],
84	                "sample_id": sample_id,
85	                "sample_sha256": sample["sha256"],
86	                "statistics": result["statistics"],
87	                "variants": result["variants"],
88	            }
89	            try:
90	                self.store.connection.execute(
91	                    "INSERT INTO runs(id, sample_id, document) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
92	                    (run_id, sample_id, self.store.encode(document)),
93	                )
94	            except Exception as error:
95	                if "UNIQUE constraint" in str(error):
96	                    raise ConflictError(f"run {run_id} already exists") from error
97	                raise
98	            return run_view(document)
99	
100	        return self._idempotent(key, f"create-run:{run_id}", create)
101	
102	    def get_run(self, run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
103	        return run_view(self._document(run_id))
104	
105	    def run_variants(self, run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
106	        variants = self._document(run_id)["variants"]
107	        return {"count": len(variants), "run_id": run_id, "variants": variants}
108	
109	    def run_export(self, run_id: str, format: str) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
110	        """Render the retained variants of a saved run; the run is unchanged."""
111	        if format == "jsonl":
112	            content_type = "application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8"
113	            variants = self._document(run_id)["variants"]
114	            body = render_jsonl(variants)
115	        elif format == "tsv":
116	            content_type = "text/tab-separated-values; charset=utf-8"
117	            variants = self._document(run_id)["variants"]
118	            body = render_tsv(variants)
119	        elif format == "vcf":
120	            content_type = "text/x-variant-call-format; charset=utf-8"
121	            document = self._document(run_id)
122	            sample = self.get_sample(document["sample_id"])
123	            body = render_vcf(document["variants"], sample["meta"])
124	        else:
125	            raise ValidationError("format must be one of jsonl, tsv, vcf")
126	        return content_type, body
127	
128	    def compare_runs(self, run_id: str, other_run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
129	        """Compare the retained ALT alleles of two finished runs; read-only."""
130	        left = self._document(run_id)
131	        right = self._document(other_run_id)
132	        left_alleles = _alleles(left)
133	        right_alleles = _alleles(right)
134	        shared_keys = left_alleles.keys() & right_alleles.keys()
135	        left_only_keys = left_alleles.keys() - right_alleles.keys()
136	        right_only_keys = right_alleles.keys() - left_alleles.keys()
137	        shared = _pick(left_alleles, shared_keys)
138	        left_only = _pick(left_alleles, left_only_keys)
139	        right_only = _pick(right_alleles, right_only_keys)
140	        buckets = (("shared", shared), ("left_only", left_only), ("right_only", right_only))
141	        return {
142	            "counts": {
143	                "left_only": len(left_only),
144	                "right_only": len(right_only),
145	                "shared": len(shared),
146	                "union": len(shared) + len(left_only) + len(right_only),
147	            },
148	            "gene_summary": _summary(buckets, lambda allele: allele["gene"] or "NA"),
149	            "impact_summary": _summary(buckets, lambda allele: allele["impact"]),
150	            "left": _side(run_id, left, left_alleles),
151	            "left_only": left_only,
152	            "right": _side(other_run_id, right, right_alleles),
153	            "right_only": right_only,
154	            "shared": shared,
155	        }
156	
157	    def cohort_runs(self, run_id: str, other_run_ids: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
158	        """Compare the retained ALT alleles of two or more runs; read-only.
159	
160	        ``other_run_ids`` is comma-joined run ids; the full path order (run_id
161	        first) is the cohort queue order.
162	        """
163	        run_ids = [run_id, *(part for part in other_run_ids.split(",") if part)]
164	        if len(run_ids) < 2:
165	            raise ValidationError("cohort requires at least two distinct runs")
166	        if len(set(run_ids)) != len(run_ids):
167	            raise ConflictError("cohort run ids must be distinct")
168	        documents = [self._document(identifier) for identifier in run_ids]
169	        per_run_alleles = [_alleles(document) for document in documents]
170	
171	        union: dict[tuple[str, int, str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}
172	        for alleles in per_run_alleles:
173	            for key, allele in alleles.items():
174	                union.setdefault(key, allele)
175	
176	        runs = [
177	            _side(identifier, document, alleles)
178	            for identifier, document, alleles in zip(run_ids, documents, per_run_alleles)
179	        ]
180	        allele_entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
181	        for key in sorted(union):
182	            present_in = [
183	                identifier
184	                for identifier, alleles in zip(run_ids, per_run_alleles)
185	                if key in alleles
186	            ]
187	            allele = dict(union[key])
188	            allele["run_count"] = len(present_in)
189	            allele["present_in"] = present_in
190	            allele_entries.append(allele)
191	
192	        run_count = len(run_ids)
193	        frequency = {str(number): 0 for number in range(1, run_count + 1)}
194	        private = {identifier: 0 for identifier in run_ids}
195	        gene_accumulator: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
196	        impact_accumulator: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
197	        core = variable = 0
198	        for allele in allele_entries:
199	            count = allele["run_count"]
200	            frequency[str(count)] += 1
201	            if count == run_count:
202	                core += 1
203	            elif count == 1:
204	                private[allele["present_in"][0]] += 1
205	            else:
206	                variable += 1
207	            for accumulator, value in (
208	                (gene_accumulator, allele["gene"] or "NA"),
209	                (impact_accumulator, allele["impact"]),
210	            ):
211	                entry = accumulator.setdefault(
212	                    value, {"core_alleles": 0, "unique_alleles": 0, "variable_alleles": 0}
213	                )
214	                entry["unique_alleles"] += 1
215	                if count == run_count:
216	                    entry["core_alleles"] += 1
217	                elif 1 < count < run_count:
218	                    entry["variable_alleles"] += 1
219	
220	        return {
221	            "alleles": allele_entries,
222	            "counts": {
223	                "unique_alleles": len(allele_entries),
224	                "core_alleles": core,
225	                "variable_alleles": variable,
226	                "private_alleles": {identifier: private[identifier] for identifier in run_ids},
227	            },
228	            "frequency_summary": frequency,
229	            "gene_summary": {key: gene_accumulator[key] for key in sorted(gene_accumulator)},
230	            "impact_summary": {key: impact_accumulator[key] for key in sorted(impact_accumulator)},
231	            "run_count": run_count,
232	            "runs": runs,
233	        }
234	
235	    def run_provenance(self, run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
236	        document = self._document(run_id)
237	        sample = self.get_sample(document["sample_id"])
238	        reproduced = execute({"records": sample["records"]}, sample["vcf"], document["params"])
239	        chain_verified = verify_chain(document["provenance"])
240	        reproduction_verified = (
241	            [entry["output_sha256"] for entry in reproduced["provenance"]]
242	            == [entry["output_sha256"] for entry in document["provenance"]]
243	            and reproduced["statistics"] == document["statistics"]
244	            and reproduced["variants"] == document["variants"]
245	        )
246	        return {
247	            "chain_verified": chain_verified,
248	            "head_sha256": document["provenance"][-1]["hash"],
249	            "reproduction_verified": reproduction_verified,
250	            "run_id": run_id,
251	            "steps": document["provenance"],

296	    """Per-key allele counts in each comparison bucket, keys sorted."""
297	    counts: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}

8	_FILEFORMAT = re.compile(r"VCFv4\.[0-9]+$")
9	_META_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$")
10	_CHROM = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$")
11	_SEQUENCE = re.compile(r"[ACGTN]+$")
12	_QUAL = re.compile(r"[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?$")
13	_FILTER_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.]+$")
14	_INFO_KEY = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*$")
15	_HEADER = ("#CHROM", "POS", "ID", "REF", "ALT", "QUAL", "FILTER", "INFO")
16	
17	
18	def parse_vcf(text: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
19	    """Parse the supported VCF subset.
20	
21	    Every structural or field-level violation raises ``ValidationError`` whose
22	    message names the offending line. Record order is preserved; ``raw`` keeps
23	    the original line so anything in the output stays traceable.
24	    """
25	    if not isinstance(text, str):
26	        raise ValidationError("vcf must be a string")
27	    lines = text.split("\n")
28	    if lines and lines[-1] == "":
29	        lines.pop()
30	    if not any(line.strip() for line in lines):
31	        raise ValidationError("vcf must not be empty")
32	
33	    meta: list[dict[str, str]] = []
34	    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
35	    chromosomes: list[str] = []
36	    seen_chromosomes: set[str] = set()
37	    seen_variants: dict[tuple[Any, ...], int] = {}
38	    header_line: int | None = None
39	    current_chromosome: str | None = None
40	    last_position = 0
41	
42	    for number, source in enumerate(lines, start=1):
43	        line = source[:-1] if source.endswith("\r") else source
44	        if not line.strip():
45	            raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: blank lines are not allowed")
46	
47	        if header_line is None:
48	            if line.startswith("##"):
49	                entry = _meta_entry(line, number)
50	                if not meta and entry["key"] != "fileformat":
51	                    raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: the first line must be a ##fileformat meta line")
52	                if entry["key"] == "fileformat" and not _FILEFORMAT.match(entry["value"]):
53	                    raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: fileformat must be VCFv4.x")
54	                meta.append(entry)
55	                continue
56	            if line.startswith("#"):
57	                if tuple(line.split("\t")) != _HEADER:
58	                    raise ValidationError(
59	                        f"line {number}: the #CHROM header must be exactly "
60	                        "#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO separated by tabs"
61	                    )
62	                header_line = number
63	                continue
64	            raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: data record appears before the #CHROM header line")
65	
66	        if line.startswith("#"):
67	            raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: header lines are not allowed after the #CHROM header")
68	
69	        record = _record(line, number)
70	        chromosome = record["chrom"]
71	        if chromosome != current_chromosome:
72	            if chromosome in seen_chromosomes:
73	                raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: chromosome {chromosome} appears in more than one block")
74	            seen_chromosomes.add(chromosome)
75	            chromosomes.append(chromosome)
76	            current_chromosome = chromosome
77	            last_position = 0
78	        if record["pos"] < last_position:
79	            raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: records must be sorted by POS within {chromosome}")
80	        last_position = record["pos"]
81	
82	        key = (chromosome, record["pos"], record["ref"], tuple(record["alts"]))
83	        if key in seen_variants:
84	            raise ValidationError(
85	                f"line {number}: duplicate variant {chromosome}:{record['pos']} "
86	                f"{record['ref']}>{','.join(record['alts'])} first appeared at line {seen_variants[key]}"
87	            )
88	        seen_variants[key] = number
89	        records.append(record)
90	
91	    if header_line is None:
92	        raise ValidationError("vcf has no #CHROM header line")
93	    if not records:
94	        raise ValidationError("vcf has no data records after the #CHROM header")
95	    return {"chromosomes": chromosomes, "meta": meta, "records": records}

98	def _meta_entry(line: str, number: int) -> dict[str, str]:
99	    key, separator, value = line[2:].partition("=")
100	    if not separator or not _META_KEY.match(key) or not value:
101	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: meta lines must look like ##key=value")
102	    return {"key": key, "raw": line, "value": value}
103	
104	
105	def _record(line: str, number: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
106	    fields = line.split("\t")
107	    if len(fields) != 8:
108	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: expected 8 tab-separated fields, found {len(fields)}")
109	    chrom, pos_text, id_text, ref_text, alt_text, qual_text, filter_text, info_text = fields
110	
111	    if not _CHROM.match(chrom):
112	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: CHROM must be a non-empty chromosome name")
113	    if not pos_text.isdigit() or int(pos_text) < 1:
114	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: POS must be a positive integer")
115	    position = int(pos_text)
116	
117	    identifier = None if id_text == "." else id_text
118	    if identifier is not None and (not identifier or any(character in identifier for character in " \t;,")):
119	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: ID must be '.' or a value without whitespace, ';' or ','")
120	
121	    reference = ref_text.upper()
122	    if not _SEQUENCE.match(reference):
123	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: REF must be a non-empty sequence of A, C, G, T or N")
124	
125	    alternates = [allele.upper() for allele in alt_text.split(",")]
126	    if any(not _SEQUENCE.match(allele) for allele in alternates):
127	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: ALT must be a comma-separated list of A, C, G, T or N sequences")
128	    if len(set(alternates)) != len(alternates):
129	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: ALT must not repeat an allele")
130	
131	    if qual_text == ".":
132	        quality: float | None = None
133	    elif _QUAL.match(qual_text):
134	        quality = float(qual_text)
135	    else:
136	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: QUAL must be '.' or a non-negative number")
137	
138	    if filter_text == ".":
139	        filters: list[str] = []
140	    else:
141	        filters = filter_text.split(";")
142	        if any(not _FILTER_TOKEN.match(token) for token in filters):
143	            raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: FILTER must be '.', 'PASS' or ';'-separated tokens")
144	        if len(set(filters)) != len(filters):
145	            raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: FILTER must not repeat a token")
146	        if "PASS" in filters and len(filters) > 1:
147	            raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: FILTER 'PASS' must not be combined with other tokens")
148	
149	    info: dict[str, str | None] = {}
150	    if info_text != ".":
151	        for entry in info_text.split(";"):
152	            key, separator, value = entry.partition("=")
153	            if not _INFO_KEY.match(key):
154	                raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: INFO entry {entry!r} does not start with a valid key")
155	            if key in info:
156	                raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: INFO key {key} is repeated")
157	            if not separator:
158	                info[key] = None
159	            elif not value or any(character.isspace() for character in value):
160	                raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: INFO {key} must have a non-empty value without whitespace")
161	            else:
162	                info[key] = value
163	
164	    if "DP" not in info:
165	        depth: int | None = None
166	    elif info["DP"] is None or not info["DP"].isdigit():
167	        raise ValidationError(f"line {number}: INFO/DP must be a non-negative integer")
168	    else:
169	        depth = int(info["DP"])
170	
171	    return {
172	        "alts": alternates,
173	        "chrom": chrom,
174	        "dp": depth,
175	        "filter": filters,
176	        "id": identifier,
177	        "info": info,
178	        "line": number,
179	        "pos": position,
180	        "qual": quality,
181	        "raw": line,
182	        "ref": reference,
183	    }

20	def digest_text(text: str) -> str:
21	    """SHA-256 of a raw UTF-8 text payload."""
22	    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
23

25	def step(
26	    number: int,
27	    name: str,
28	    params: dict[str, Any],
29	    input_sha256: str,
30	    output_sha256: str,
31	    previous_sha256: str | None,
32	) -> dict[str, Any]:
33	    """Build one provenance link; its hash covers the previous link's hash."""
34	    body = {
35	        "step": number,
36	        "name": name,
37	        "params": params,
38	        "input_sha256": input_sha256,
39	        "output_sha256": output_sha256,
40	        "previous_sha256": previous_sha256,
41	    }
42	    return {**body, "hash": digest(body)}
43	
44	
45	def verify_chain(steps: Any) -> bool:
46	    """Recompute every link hash and the chain linkage."""
47	    if not isinstance(steps, list) or not steps:
48	        return False
49	    previous: str | None = None
50	    for number, entry in enumerate(steps, start=1):
51	        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(STEP_FIELDS) | {"hash"}:
52	            return False
53	        if entry["step"] != number or entry["previous_sha256"] != previous:
54	            return False
55	        body = {field: entry[field] for field in STEP_FIELDS}
56	        if digest(body) != entry["hash"]:
57	            return False
58	        previous = entry["hash"]
59	    return True

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

from .errors import ValidationError

_IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,99}$")


def identifier(value: Any, field: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not _IDENTIFIER.match(value):
        raise ValidationError(
            f"{field} must match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{{0,99}}"
        )
    return value


def sample_view(document: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Public projection of a stored sample; no timestamps, fully deterministic."""
    return {
        "chromosomes": list(document["chromosomes"]),
        "id": document["id"],
        "meta_lines": len(document["meta"]),
        "records": len(document["records"]),
        "sha256": document["sha256"],
    }


def run_view(document: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Public projection of a stored run."""
    provenance = document["provenance"]
    return {
        "id": document["id"],
        "params": document["params"],
        "provenance_head": provenance[-1]["hash"],
        "provenance_length": len(provenance),
        "sample_id": document["sample_id"],
        "sample_sha256": document["sample_sha256"],
        "statistics": document["statistics"],
        "status": "succeeded",
    }

import json
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

from variantrail.errors import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationError
from variantrail.export import TSV_HEADER
from variantrail.server import Handler
from variantrail.service import VariantRail

HEADER = "#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO"
PREAMBLE = "##fileformat=VCFv4.2\n##reference=GRCh38\n##contig=<ID=chr1>"

# Lines 5-11 of VCF hold the data records used by most tests.
VCF = "\n".join(
    [
        PREAMBLE,
        HEADER,
        "chr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42",
        "chr1\t11856378\trs2\tG\tT\t20\tPASS\tDP=42",
        "chr1\t11856379\t.\tA\tG\t.\tq10\tDP=5",
        "chr7\t55019017\t.\tG\tGA\t50\tPASS\tDP=31",
        "chr7\t55019017\t.\tG\tT\t50\tPASS\t.",
        "chr12\t25245350\t.\tC\tA,T\t80\tPASS\tDP=60",
        "chr17\t43093445\t.\tC\tT\t99\tPASS\tDP=55",
    ]
) + "\n"


def single(chrom="chr1", pos=11856378, ref="G", alt="A", qual="60", filter_value="PASS", info="DP=42"):
    return "\n".join([PREAMBLE, HEADER, f"{chrom}\t{pos}\t.\t{ref}\t{alt}\t{qual}\t{filter_value}\t{info}"]) + "\n"


class VariantRailTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.service = VariantRail(str(Path(self.directory.name) / "test.db"))

    def tearDown(self):
        self.directory.cleanup()

    def sample(self, key="s1", vcf=VCF, sample_id="s1"):
        return self.service.create_sample({"id": sample_id, "vcf": vcf}, key)

    def start_run(self, params=None, key="r1", run_id="run-1", sample_id="s1"):
        body = {"id": run_id}
        if params is not None:
            body["params"] = params
        return self.service.create_run(sample_id, body, key)

    # --- ingestion ---------------------------------------------------------

    def test_sample_parses_headers_and_reports_shape(self):
        created = self.sample()
        self.assertEqual(
            {"chromosomes": ["chr1", "chr7", "chr12", "chr17"], "id": "s1", "meta_lines": 3, "records": 7},
            {key: value for key, value in created.items() if key != "sha256"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(64, len(created["sha256"]))

    def test_sample_carries_its_own_record_and_meta_lines(self):
        self.sample()
        document = self.service.get_sample("s1")
        self.assertEqual(3, len(document["meta"]))
        self.assertEqual("##fileformat=VCFv4.2", document["meta"][0]["raw"])
        self.assertEqual("VCFv4.2", document["meta"][0]["value"])
        self.assertEqual("GRCh38", document["meta"][1]["value"])
        self.assertEqual("chr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42", document["records"][0]["raw"])
        self.assertEqual(5, document["records"][0]["line"])

    def test_lowercase_sequence_fields_are_normalised(self):
        self.sample(vcf=single(ref="g", alt="a"))
        document = self.service.get_sample("s1")
        self.assertEqual("G", document["records"][0]["ref"])
        self.assertEqual(["A"], document["records"][0]["alts"])

    def test_crlf_line_endings_are_accepted(self):
        created = self.sample(vcf=VCF.replace("\n", "\r\n"))
        self.assertEqual(7, created["records"])

    def test_missing_trailing_newline_is_accepted(self):
        created = self.sample(vcf=VCF.rstrip("\n"))
        self.assertEqual(7, created["records"])

    def test_invalid_vcf_reports_the_line_number(self):
        header_only = PREAMBLE + "\n" + HEADER
        cases = [
            ("chr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t.\tPASS\t.", "line 1"),
            ("##reference=GRCh38\n" + HEADER + "\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t.\tPASS\t.", "line 1"),
            ("##fileformat=VCFv3.0\n" + HEADER + "\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t.\tPASS\t.", "line 1"),
            (PREAMBLE + "\n#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t.\tPASS\t.", "line 4"),
            (header_only + "\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t.\tPASS", "line 5"),
            (header_only + "\nchr1\t0\t.\tA\tG\t.\tPASS\t.", "line 5"),
            (header_only + "\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\tabc\tPASS\t.", "line 5"),
            (header_only + "\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\t<DEL>\t5\tPASS\t.", "line 5"),
            (header_only + "\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\tDP=1;DP=2", "line 5"),
            (header_only + "\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\tDP=x", "line 5"),
            (header_only + "\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS;q10\t.", "line 5"),
            (header_only + "\n\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t.", "line 5"),
            (header_only + "\n##extra=1\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t.", "line 5"),
            ("##fileformat=VCFv4.2\n" + HEADER + "\n##extra=1\nchr1\t1\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t.", "line 3"),
        ]
        for vcf, pattern in cases:
            with self.subTest(vcf=vcf), self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, pattern):
                self.sample(vcf=vcf, key=f"k-{pattern}-{len(vcf)}")

    def test_structural_vcf_failures_are_rejected(self):
        for vcf, pattern in [
            (PREAMBLE, "no #CHROM header"),
            (PREAMBLE + "\n" + HEADER + "\n", "no data records"),
            ("   \n", "must not be empty"),
        ]:
            with self.subTest(vcf=vcf), self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, pattern):
                self.sample(vcf=vcf)

    def test_unordered_and_duplicate_variants_are_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "sorted by POS"):
            self.sample(vcf="\n".join([PREAMBLE, HEADER, "chr1\t200\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t.", "chr1\t100\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t."]))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "duplicate variant"):
            self.sample(vcf="\n".join([PREAMBLE, HEADER, "chr1\t100\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t.", "chr1\t100\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t."]))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "more than one block"):
            self.sample(
                vcf="\n".join(
                    [
                        PREAMBLE,
                        HEADER,
                        "chr1\t100\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t.",
                        "chr2\t100\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t.",
                        "chr1\t200\t.\tA\tG\t5\tPASS\t.",
                    ]
                )
            )

    def test_sample_body_and_identifier_are_validated(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "exactly id and vcf"):

        self.assertEqual(400, status)
        self.assertEqual("cohort requires at least two distinct runs", json.loads(body)["error"]["message"])
        status, _, body = self.get("/runs/run-1/cohort")
        self.assertEqual(400, status)
        error = json.loads(body)["error"]
        self.assertEqual("validation_error", error["code"])
        self.assertEqual("cohort requires at least two distinct runs", error["message"])
        status, _, body = self.get("/runs/run-1/cohort/run-1")
        self.assertEqual(409, status)
        error = json.loads(body)["error"]
        self.assertEqual("conflict", error["code"])
        self.assertEqual("cohort run ids must be distinct", error["message"])
        status, _, body = self.get("/runs/run-1/cohort/run-2,run-2")
        self.assertEqual(409, status)
        self.assertEqual("cohort run ids must be distinct", json.loads(body)["error"]["message"])
        status, _, body = self.get("/runs/run-1/cohort/missing")
        self.assertEqual(404, status)
        error = json.loads(body)["error"]
        self.assertEqual("not_found", error["code"])
        self.assertEqual("run missing was not found", error["message"])
        status, _, body = self.get("/runs/missing/cohort/run-1")
        self.assertEqual(404, status)
        self.assertEqual("run missing was not found", json.loads(body)["error"]["message"])
        # Duplicate takes precedence over the missing id.
        status, _, body = self.get("/runs/run-1/cohort/missing,run-1")
        self.assertEqual(409, status)
        self.assertEqual("cohort run ids must be distinct", json.loads(body)["error"]["message"])

    def test_cohort_and_compare_endpoints_coexist(self):
        status, _, body = self.get("/runs/run-1/compare/run-2")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual({"left_only", "right_only", "shared"}, set(json.loads(body)) - {"counts", "left", "right", "gene_summary", "impact_summary"})
        status, _, cohort_body = self.get("/runs/run-1/cohort/run-2")
        self.assertEqual(200, status)
        self.assertEqual(
            {"run_count", "runs", "alleles", "counts", "frequency_summary", "gene_summary", "impact_summary"},
            set(json.loads(cohort_body)),
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

content.content:
1	# VariantRail
2	
3	VariantRail is a small backend for a genome variant annotation pipeline with a
4	reproducible provenance trail. It ingests a VCF subset, filters records by
5	quality and depth, annotates every ALT allele with a built-in gene/consequence
6	table, summarises the result, and records one SHA-256 link per pipeline step so
7	any run can be re-derived and checked byte for byte.
8	
9	The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:
10	
11	- a sample is VCF text that is parsed and validated at upload time;
12	- a run replays four fixed steps: `ingest`, `filter`, `annotate`, `summarize`;
13	- each step stores the hash of its input, the hash of its output, and the
14	  previous link's hash, so the trail is a chain;
15	- hashes depend only on content and parameters, never on the sample id, the
16	  run id, wall-clock time, or process state;
17	- the annotation table is built in and its content hash is itself a
18	  provenance input;
19	- every output variant keeps the original VCF line verbatim.
20	
21	## Requirements
22	
23	- Python 3.11 or newer
24	- no third-party runtime dependencies
25	
26	## Run the service
27	
28	```bash
29	PYTHONPATH=src python -m variantrail.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18083 --database variantrail.db
30	```
31	
32	The process prints `VariantRail listening on http://127.0.0.1:18083` after it
33	has bound the port.
34	
35	## HTTP API
36	
37	All request and response bodies are JSON except the `jsonl`, `tsv` and `vcf`
38	run export endpoints, and unknown fields are rejected. Both `POST` endpoints
39	require an `Idempotency-Key` header; repeating a key returns the stored first
40	response verbatim, and reusing a key for another operation is a `conflict`.
41	
42	### Health
43	
44	`GET /health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.
45	
46	### Create a sample
47	
48	```http
49	POST /samples
50	Idempotency-Key: sample-1
51	Content-Type: application/json
52	
53	{"id":"trio-1","vcf":"##fileformat=VCFv4.2\n##reference=GRCh38\n#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO\nchr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42\nchr1\t11856378\trs2\tG\tT\t20\tPASS\tDP=42\nchr7\t55019017\t.\tG\tGA\t50\tPASS\tDP=31\nchr17\t43093445\t.\tC\tT\t99\tPASS\tDP=55\n"}
54	```
55	
56	Returns HTTP 201 with a deterministic projection of the parsed sample:
57	
58	```json
59	{"chromosomes":["chr1","chr7","chr17"],"id":"trio-1","meta_lines":2,"records":4,
60	 "sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef"}
61	```
62	
63	`sha256` is the SHA-256 of the uploaded VCF text. `id` must match
64	`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,99}` and is unique (`conflict` otherwise).
65	
66	### The supported VCF subset
67	
68	The text is split on `\n`; one trailing newline is optional and a single
69	trailing `\r` per line is ignored, so CRLF files are accepted. Every violation
70	raises `validation_error` with a message shaped `line <n>: ...`.
71	
72	1. The first line must be `##fileformat=VCFv4.<digits>`.
73	2. Zero or more `##key=value` meta lines follow, `key` matching
74	   `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*` and `value` non-empty.
75	3. Exactly one `#CHROM` line follows whose tab-separated columns are exactly
76	   `#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO`. `FORMAT` and sample columns are
77	   not supported and are rejected.
78	4. One or more data lines follow, each with exactly 8 tab-separated fields:
79	   - `CHROM` matches `[A-Za-z0-9_.]+`; chromosome blocks must be contiguous, so
80	     a chromosome may not reappear once another chromosome started;
81	   - `POS` is a positive integer and non-decreasing within a chromosome, and
82	     `(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT)` is unique in the file;
83	   - `ID` is `.` (becomes `null`) or a value without whitespace, `;` or `,`;
84	   - `REF` is a non-empty `[ACGTN]+` sequence;
85	   - `ALT` is one or more `[ACGTN]+` sequences separated by `,` without
86	     repeats; symbolic alleles such as `<DEL>` or `*` are rejected;
87	   - `REF` and `ALT` are upper-cased before storage;
88	   - `QUAL` is `.` (becomes `null`) or a non-negative decimal number;
89	   - `FILTER` is `.` (empty list), `PASS`, or `;`-separated tokens matching
90	     `[A-Za-z0-9_.]+`; `PASS` must not be combined with another token;
91	   - `INFO` is `.` (empty object) or `;`-separated `KEY` / `KEY=VALUE` entries
92	     with `KEY` matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*`, no repeated keys and a
93	     non-empty whitespace-free value; `DP`, when present, must be a
94	     non-negative integer.
95	
96	Blank lines, header lines after the first data record, a missing `#CHROM`
97	header, and a file with no data records are rejected.
98	
99	### Start a run
100	
101	```http
102	POST /samples/trio-1/runs
103	Idempotency-Key: run-1
104	Content-Type: application/json
105	
106	{"id":"run-1","params":{"min_qual":30,"min_dp":10,"pass_only":true,"genes":["MTHFR","EGFR","BRCA1"]}}
107	```
108	
109	`params` is optional; the body must contain `id` and may contain only `params`
110	besides it. The run executes synchronously, so a returned run is always
111	`succeeded`. Returns HTTP 201:
112	
113	```json
114	{"id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1",
115	 "sample_sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef",
116	 "params":{"genes":["BRCA1","EGFR","MTHFR"],"impacts":[],"min_dp":10,"min_qual":30.0,"pass_only":true},
117	 "status":"succeeded","provenance_length":4,
118	 "provenance_head":"40807a2cebf5110a5a3be231ab78ca690823b9def8414dd373314354cac65b40",
119	 "statistics":{"records_total":4,"records_kept":3,"records_filtered":1,
120	   "filter_counts":{"allele_filtered":0,"dp_below_min":0,"not_pass":0,"qual_below_min":1},
121	   "alleles_total":4,"alleles_kept":3,
122	   "consequence_counts":{"frameshift_variant":1,"missense_variant":1,"stop_gained":1},
123	   "impact_counts":{"HIGH":2,"MODERATE":1},
124	   "gene_counts":{"BRCA1":1,"EGFR":1,"MTHFR":1}}}
125	```
126	
127	### Run parameters
128	
129	Every key is optional and the stored `params` object always contains all five.
130	`genes` and `impacts` are stored sorted, so request order never changes a hash.
131	
132	- `pass_only` (boolean, default `false`) — keep only records whose `FILTER` is
133	  exactly `["PASS"]`.
134	- `min_qual` (non-negative finite number, default `0.0`, stored as a float) —
135	  keep records with `QUAL >= min_qual`.
136	- `min_dp` (non-negative integer, default `0`) — keep records with
137	  `DP >= min_dp`.
138	- `genes` (array of non-empty strings, default `[]` = no restriction) — after
139	  annotation keep only alleles whose gene is listed. An allele with no table
140	  match has gene `null` and is dropped when `genes` is non-empty.
141	- `impacts` (array, default `[]` = no restriction) — after annotation keep only
142	  alleles whose impact is listed; values must come from `HIGH`, `MODERATE`,
143	  `LOW`, `MODIFIER`, `UNKNOWN`.
144	
145	A record that passed the record-level filters but whose alleles are all removed
146	by `genes`/`impacts` is dropped as well.
147	
148	### Filter accounting and statistics
149	
150	`filter_counts` attributes every filtered record to exactly one reason, in this
151	precedence: `not_pass` (`pass_only` set and `FILTER` is not `["PASS"]`);
152	`qual_below_min` (`QUAL` below `min_qual`, or `null` while `min_qual > 0`);
153	`dp_below_min` (`DP` below `min_dp`, or `null` while `min_dp > 0`);
154	`allele_filtered` (survived the first three but no allele survived the
155	allowlists). Hence `records_filtered == sum(filter_counts.values())` and
156	`records_kept == records_total - records_filtered` always hold.
157	
158	`alleles_total` counts every ALT allele of every record and `alleles_kept`
159	counts the alleles present in the run's variants. `gene_counts` uses the key
160	`NA` for alleles with no table match. `consequence_counts`, `impact_counts` and
161	`gene_counts` omit zero counts and are sorted by key.
162	
163	### Get a run
164	
165	`GET /runs/run-1` returns the run document shown above.
166	
167	### Get run variants
168	
169	`GET /runs/run-1/variants` returns `{"count":<n>,"run_id":"run-1","variants":[...]}`
170	in file order. Each variant repeats the parsed fields plus `raw`, the original
171	line, so every output stays traceable to the input:
172	
173	```json
174	{"alts":["A"],
175	 "annotations":[{"allele":"A","allele_index":1,"consequence":"missense_variant","gene":"MTHFR","impact":"MODERATE"}],
176	 "chrom":"chr1","dp":42,"filter":["PASS"],"id":"rs1","info":{"DP":"42"},"line":4,
177	 "pos":11856378,"qual":60.0,"raw":"chr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42","ref":"G"}
178	```
179	
180	`line` is the 1-based line of the record in the uploaded VCF and `allele_index`
181	is the 1-based VCF ALT index.
182	
183	### Export run results
184	
185	`GET /runs/run-1/exports/jsonl`, `GET /runs/run-1/exports/tsv` and
186	`GET /runs/run-1/exports/vcf` hand the
187	retained variants of a saved run to downstream analysis as a stable payload.
188	The body is generated on demand from the stored run; it is never written to
189	disk, and the run, its variants and its provenance are not modified.
190	
191	`jsonl` is served as `application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8`: one variant object
192	per line in the original file order, using the same fields and values as
193	`GET /runs/{run_id}/variants`. Each line is UTF-8 JSON with no indentation and
194	keys sorted lexicographically, terminated by a single LF; the body ends with
195	the last line's LF (no trailing blank line). A run with no variants returns an
196	empty body.
197	
198	`tsv` is served as `text/tab-separated-values; charset=utf-8` and always opens
199	with the fixed header:
200	
201	```
202	chrom	pos	id	ref	alt	allele_index	gene	consequence	impact	qual	dp	filter	info	line
203	```
204	
205	Each retained annotation is one row, so a record with several retained ALT
206	alleles spans several rows; variant file order and annotation order are kept.
207	Formatting rules:
208	
209	- `id`, `gene`, `qual` or `dp` is `NA` when null; `qual` otherwise keeps the
210	  JSON decimal form (e.g. `60.0`);
211	- an empty `FILTER` is `.`; several filters are joined with `;`;
212	- `INFO` is `;`-joined `KEY=VALUE` pairs sorted by key; bare flags are written
213	  as `KEY`; empty INFO is `.`;
214	- numbers use the JSON decimal representation and text is not quoted.
215	
216	A run with no variants returns just the header line. An unknown `run_id`
217	returns 404 `not_found`; any `format` other than `jsonl`, `tsv` or `vcf`
218	returns 400 `validation_error`, both with the standard error object.
219	
220	`vcf` is served as `text/x-variant-call-format; charset=utf-8`: the retained
221	variants rendered back as VCF v4.2 text (UTF-8, LF line endings). The header
222	opens with `##fileformat=VCFv4.2`, repeats the uploaded sample's other meta
223	lines in their original order, adds `##source=variantrail`, and declares four
224	export INFO keys — `ALLELE_INDEX` (Integer), `VT_GENE`, `VT_CONSEQUENCE` and
225	`VT_IMPACT` (String, all `Number=1`) — before the tab-separated
226	`#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO` column header. Each retained ALT
227	allele is one record, in variant file order and `allele_index` order, with
228	`ALT` holding only the current allele. `ID`, `QUAL` and an empty `FILTER` are
229	`.` when missing; `INFO` lists the original entries sorted by key, then the
230	four export keys (`VT_GENE` is `NA` when no gene is annotated). If an original
231	INFO field uses `ALLELE_INDEX` or one of the `VT_*` keys, the export returns
232	400 `validation_error` naming the conflicting key. A run with no variants
233	returns just the header, and repeated requests are byte-identical.
234	
235	### Compare two runs
236	
237	`GET /runs/{run_id}/compare/{other_run_id}` compares the retained ALT alleles
238	of two finished runs — `run_id` on the left, `other_run_id` on the right. It
239	only reads the stored runs: no pipeline step is re-executed and neither run,
240	its variants, its exports, nor its provenance is modified. The runs may belong
241	to different samples. No `Idempotency-Key` is required.
242	
243	An allele's identity is the tuple `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)`; duplicates of the
244	same identity within one run count once. Returns HTTP 200:
245	
246	```json
247	{"left":{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":8},
248	 "right":{"run_id":"run-2","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":4},
249	 "counts":{"shared":4,"left_only":4,"right_only":0,"union":8},
250	 "shared":[{"chrom":"chr1","pos":11856378,"ref":"G","alt":"T",
251	   "gene":"MTHFR","consequence":"stop_gained","impact":"HIGH"}],
252	 "left_only":[...],
253	 "right_only":[...],
254	 "gene_summary":{"MTHFR":{"shared":1,"left_only":1,"right_only":0}},
255	 "impact_summary":{"HIGH":{"shared":4,"left_only":0,"right_only":0}}}
256	```
257	
258	- `shared`, `left_only` and `right_only` hold every distinct allele on both
259	  sides, on the left only, and on the right only; each element carries
260	  `chrom`, `pos`, `ref`, `alt`, `gene`, `consequence` and `impact`, with
261	  `gene` kept as JSON `null` when the allele has no table match. Comparing a
262	  run with itself puts every allele in `shared`.
263	- Each array is sorted by `chrom` (text order), then `pos` (numeric), then
264	  `ref`, then `alt`, so repeated requests are byte-for-byte identical.
265	- `counts` mirrors the three array lengths plus `union`, their total.
266	- `gene_summary` and `impact_summary` count the alleles of each bucket per
267	  gene and per impact; keys are sorted lexicographically, a `null` gene
268	  appears as `NA`, and impacts keep their original values.
269	
270	An unknown `run_id` or `other_run_id` returns 404 `not_found` with the
271	message `run <run_id> was not found`.
272	
273	### Compare a cohort of runs
274	
275	`GET /runs/{run_id}/cohort/{other_run_ids}` compares the retained ALT alleles
276	of two or more finished runs at once. `other_run_ids` is two or more run ids
277	joined with commas; the path order (the path `run_id` first, then the comma
278	list) is the cohort queue order. Like the two-run comparison it only reads the
279	stored runs: no pipeline step is re-executed and no run, variant, export or
280	provenance record is modified. No `Idempotency-Key` is required.
281	
282	An allele's identity is again `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)`; duplicates of the same
283	identity within one run count once, and annotations are taken as stored — no
284	filtering or re-annotation happens. Returns HTTP 200:
285	
286	```json
287	{"run_count":3,
288	 "runs":[{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":8},
289	         {"run_id":"run-2","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":4},
290	         {"run_id":"run-3","sample_id":"trio-2","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":3}],
291	 "alleles":[{"chrom":"chr1","pos":11856378,"ref":"G","alt":"A","gene":"MTHFR",
292	   "consequence":"missense_variant","impact":"MODERATE","run_count":2,
293	   "present_in":["run-1","run-3"]}],
294	 "counts":{"unique_alleles":9,"core_alleles":2,"variable_alleles":3,
295	   "private_alleles":{"run-1":3,"run-2":1,"run-3":0}},
296	 "frequency_summary":{"1":4,"2":3,"3":2},
297	 "gene_summary":{"BRCA1":{"unique_alleles":1,"core_alleles":1,"variable_alleles":0},
298	                "MTHFR":{"unique_alleles":2,"core_alleles":0,"variable_alleles":2}},
299	 "impact_summary":{"HIGH":{"unique_alleles":4,"core_alleles":2,"variable_alleles":2}}}
300	```
301	
302	- `runs` repeats the queued runs in queue order; each entry has `run_id`,
303	  `sample_id`, `sample_sha256` and `allele_count`, the number of distinct
304	  retained alleles in that run.
305	- `alleles` holds every distinct allele of the union (different ALTs at the
306	  same coordinate are separate entries). Each element carries `chrom`, `pos`,
307	  `ref`, `alt`, `gene` (`null` when the allele has no table match),
308	  `consequence`, `impact`, `run_count` — the number of cohort runs containing
309	  it — and `present_in`, the run ids of those runs in queue order. The array
310	  is sorted by `chrom` (text order), then `pos` (numeric), then `ref`, then
311	  `alt`, so repeated requests are byte-for-byte identical.
312	- `counts.unique_alleles` is the total number of entries in `alleles`;
313	  `core_alleles` counts alleles present in all `run_count` runs,
314	  `variable_alleles` alleles present in between 2 and `run_count - 1` runs,
315	  and `private_alleles` breaks the alleles present in exactly one run down by
316	  `run_id`, in queue order (runs without a private allele show `0`).
317	- `frequency_summary` has the string keys `"1"` through
318	  `"<run_count>"` and counts alleles present in exactly that many runs, with
319	  missing frequencies filled in as `0`.
320	- `gene_summary` and `impact_summary` group `unique_alleles`, `core_alleles`
321	  and `variable_alleles` per gene and per impact; a `null` gene appears as
322	  `NA`, categories with no alleles are omitted, and keys are sorted
323	  lexicographically. Private alleles are not separately listed there
324	  (`unique = core + variable + private`).
325	
326	Changing the queue order returns the same data apart from the order of `runs`
327	and of each `present_in`; the allele set, counts and summaries are unchanged,
328	and repeating a request is byte-identical.
329	
330	Fewer than two run ids in the path is a 400 `validation_error` with the
331	message `cohort requires at least two distinct runs`; a repeated run id is a
332	409 `conflict` with the message `cohort run ids must be distinct`; any run id
333	that does not exist is a 404 `not_found` with the message
334	`run <run_id> was not found`.
335	
336	### The annotation table
337	
338	Annotation matches the exact tuple `(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT)`. A variant with no
339	matching row is annotated `gene: null`, `consequence: "intergenic_variant"`,
340	`impact: "MODIFIER"`.
341	
342	```
343	chr1  11856378  G  A    MTHFR  missense_variant       MODERATE
344	chr1  11856378  G  T    MTHFR  stop_gained            HIGH
345	chr7  55019017  G  GA   EGFR   frameshift_variant     HIGH
346	chr7  55019017  G  T    EGFR   stop_gained            HIGH
347	chr7  55273000  C  T    EGFR   synonymous_variant     LOW
348	chr11 5227002   T  C    HBB    missense_variant       MODERATE
349	chr12 25245350  C  A    KRAS   missense_variant       MODERATE
350	chr12 25245350  C  T    KRAS   missense_variant       MODERATE
351	chr12 25245351  C  T    KRAS   splice_donor_variant   HIGH
352	chr17 43093445  C  T    BRCA1  stop_gained            HIGH
353	chr17 43093446  A  G    BRCA1  missense_variant       MODERATE
354	chr17 7676154   C  T    TP53   missense_variant       MODERATE
355	chr19 11200138  C  T    LDLR   missense_variant       MODERATE
356	chrX  31137345  A  G    DMD    missense_variant       MODERATE
357	```
358	
359	This is a small synthetic table with GRCh38-style chromosome names and real gene
360	symbols; the coordinates are illustrative and it is not a clinical annotation
361	source.
362	
363	### Get run provenance
364	
365	`GET /runs/run-1/provenance` returns `{"run_id","verified","chain_verified",
366	"reproduction_verified","head_sha256","steps":[...]}`, where a step looks like:
367	
368	```json
369	{"step":1,"name":"ingest","params":{"parser_version":"variantrail-vcf-1"},
370	 "input_sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef",
371	 "output_sha256":"0f5d73dd61762cefc2df233d1e604de50d21df017a6f9e5608851a3c700c6103",
372	 "previous_sha256":null,
373	 "hash":"6de42193fc25e82afb9c32b0d6170629b69eb25268d978864f9162b27ed75530"}
374	```
375	
376	Write `canonical(x)` for `json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",",":"),
377	sort_keys=True)` and `H(x)` for the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the UTF-8
378	bytes of `canonical(x)`. The four links are:
379	
380	| step | name | params | input_sha256 | output_sha256 |
381	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
382	| 1 | `ingest` | `{"parser_version":"variantrail-vcf-1"}` | SHA-256 of the VCF text | `H({"records":<parsed records>})` |
383	| 2 | `filter` | `min_dp`, `min_qual`, `pass_only` | step 1 `output_sha256` | `H({"filter_counts":<3 record keys>,"records":<kept records>})` |
384	| 3 | `annotate` | `annotation_table_sha256`, `genes`, `impacts` | step 2 `output_sha256` | `H({"filter_counts":<4 keys>,"variants":<variants>})` |
385	| 4 | `summarize` | `{}` | step 3 `output_sha256` | `H(<statistics>)` |
386	
387	Each link's own hash covers the previous link, so the trail is tamper-evident:
388	
389	```
390	body = {step, name, params, input_sha256, output_sha256, previous_sha256}
391	hash = H(body)                 # previous_sha256 is null for step 1
392	```
393	
394	`chain_verified` recomputes every link hash and checks that each
395	`previous_sha256` equals the previous link's `hash`. `reproduction_verified`
396	re-reads the stored sample VCF, re-executes all four steps with the stored
397	`params`, and compares the four `output_sha256` values, the statistics and the
398	variants. `verified` is the conjunction of both; the endpoint never rewrites the
399	stored trail.
400	
401	## Errors
402	
403	```json
404	{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"line 5: POS must be a positive integer"}}
405	```
406	
407	Validation errors return 400, missing resources 404, conflicts 409. A missing
408	`Idempotency-Key` header is a `validation_error`, and reusing one key for a
409	different operation is a `conflict`.
410	
411	## Tests
412	
413	```bash
414	PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
415	```

file.content:
# VariantRail

VariantRail is a small backend for a genome variant annotation pipeline with a
reproducible provenance trail. It ingests a VCF subset, filters records by
quality and depth, annotates every ALT allele with a built-in gene/consequence
table, summarises the result, and records one SHA-256 link per pipeline step so
any run can be re-derived and checked byte for byte.

The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:

- a sample is VCF text that is parsed and validated at upload time;
- a run replays four fixed steps: `ingest`, `filter`, `annotate`, `summarize`;
- each step stores the hash of its input, the hash of its output, and the
  previous link's hash, so the trail is a chain;
- hashes depend only on content and parameters, never on the sample id, the
  run id, wall-clock time, or process state;
- the annotation table is built in and its content hash is itself a
  provenance input;
- every output variant keeps the original VCF line verbatim.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- no third-party runtime dependencies

## Run the service

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m variantrail.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18083 --database variantrail.db
```

The process prints `VariantRail listening on http://127.0.0.1:18083` after it
has bound the port.

## HTTP API

All request and response bodies are JSON except the `jsonl`, `tsv` and `vcf`
run export endpoints, and unknown fields are rejected. Both `POST` endpoints
require an `Idempotency-Key` header; repeating a key returns the stored first
response verbatim, and reusing a key for another operation is a `conflict`.

### Health

`GET /health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

### Create a sample

```http
POST /samples
Idempotency-Key: sample-1
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"trio-1","vcf":"##fileformat=VCFv4.2\n##reference=GRCh38\n#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO\nchr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42\nchr1\t11856378\trs2\tG\tT\t20\tPASS\tDP=42\nchr7\t55019017\t.\tG\tGA\t50\tPASS\tDP=31\nchr17\t43093445\t.\tC\tT\t99\tPASS\tDP=55\n"}
```

Returns HTTP 201 with a deterministic projection of the parsed sample:

```json
{"chromosomes":["chr1","chr7","chr17"],"id":"trio-1","meta_lines":2,"records":4,
 "sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef"}
```

`sha256` is the SHA-256 of the uploaded VCF text. `id` must match
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,99}` and is unique (`conflict` otherwise).

### The supported VCF subset

The text is split on `\n`; one trailing newline is optional and a single
trailing `\r` per line is ignored, so CRLF files are accepted. Every violation
raises `validation_error` with a message shaped `line <n>: ...`.

1. The first line must be `##fileformat=VCFv4.<digits>`.
2. Zero or more `##key=value` meta lines follow, `key` matching
   `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*` and `value` non-empty.
3. Exactly one `#CHROM` line follows whose tab-separated columns are exactly
   `#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO`. `FORMAT` and sample columns are
   not supported and are rejected.
4. One or more data lines follow, each with exactly 8 tab-separated fields:
   - `CHROM` matches `[A-Za-z0-9_.]+`; chromosome blocks must be contiguous, so
     a chromosome may not reappear once another chromosome started;
   - `POS` is a positive integer and non-decreasing within a chromosome, and
     `(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT)` is unique in the file;
   - `ID` is `.` (becomes `null`) or a value without whitespace, `;` or `,`;
   - `REF` is a non-empty `[ACGTN]+` sequence;
   - `ALT` is one or more `[ACGTN]+` sequences separated by `,` without
     repeats; symbolic alleles such as `<DEL>` or `*` are rejected;
   - `REF` and `ALT` are upper-cased before storage;
   - `QUAL` is `.` (becomes `null`) or a non-negative decimal number;
   - `FILTER` is `.` (empty list), `PASS`, or `;`-separated tokens matching
     `[A-Za-z0-9_.]+`; `PASS` must not be combined with another token;
   - `INFO` is `.` (empty object) or `;`-separated `KEY` / `KEY=VALUE` entries
     with `KEY` matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*`, no repeated keys and a
     non-empty whitespace-free value; `DP`, when present, must be a
     non-negative integer.

Blank lines, header lines after the first data record, a missing `#CHROM`
header, and a file with no data records are rejected.

### Start a run

```http
POST /samples/trio-1/runs
Idempotency-Key: run-1
Content-Type: application/json

{"id":"run-1","params":{"min_qual":30,"min_dp":10,"pass_only":true,"genes":["MTHFR","EGFR","BRCA1"]}}
```

`params` is optional; the body must contain `id` and may contain only `params`
besides it. The run executes synchronously, so a returned run is always
`succeeded`. Returns HTTP 201:

```json
{"id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1",
 "sample_sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef",
 "params":{"genes":["BRCA1","EGFR","MTHFR"],"impacts":[],"min_dp":10,"min_qual":30.0,"pass_only":true},
 "status":"succeeded","provenance_length":4,
 "provenance_head":"40807a2cebf5110a5a3be231ab78ca690823b9def8414dd373314354cac65b40",
 "statistics":{"records_total":4,"records_kept":3,"records_filtered":1,
   "filter_counts":{"allele_filtered":0,"dp_below_min":0,"not_pass":0,"qual_below_min":1},
   "alleles_total":4,"alleles_kept":3,
   "consequence_counts":{"frameshift_variant":1,"missense_variant":1,"stop_gained":1},
   "impact_counts":{"HIGH":2,"MODERATE":1},
   "gene_counts":{"BRCA1":1,"EGFR":1,"MTHFR":1}}}
```

### Run parameters

Every key is optional and the stored `params` object always contains all five.
`genes` and `impacts` are stored sorted, so request order never changes a hash.

- `pass_only` (boolean, default `false`) — keep only records whose `FILTER` is
  exactly `["PASS"]`.
- `min_qual` (non-negative finite number, default `0.0`, stored as a float) —
  keep records with `QUAL >= min_qual`.
- `min_dp` (non-negative integer, default `0`) — keep records with
  `DP >= min_dp`.
- `genes` (array of non-empty strings, default `[]` = no restriction) — after
  annotation keep only alleles whose gene is listed. An allele with no table
  match has gene `null` and is dropped when `genes` is non-empty.
- `impacts` (array, default `[]` = no restriction) — after annotation keep only
  alleles whose impact is listed; values must come from `HIGH`, `MODERATE`,
  `LOW`, `MODIFIER`, `UNKNOWN`.

A record that passed the record-level filters but whose alleles are all removed
by `genes`/`impacts` is dropped as well.

### Filter accounting and statistics

`filter_counts` attributes every filtered record to exactly one reason, in this
precedence: `not_pass` (`pass_only` set and `FILTER` is not `["PASS"]`);
`qual_below_min` (`QUAL` below `min_qual`, or `null` while `min_qual > 0`);
`dp_below_min` (`DP` below `min_dp`, or `null` while `min_dp > 0`);
`allele_filtered` (survived the first three but no allele survived the
allowlists). Hence `records_filtered == sum(filter_counts.values())` and
`records_kept == records_total - records_filtered` always hold.

`alleles_total` counts every ALT allele of every record and `alleles_kept`
counts the alleles present in the run's variants. `gene_counts` uses the key
`NA` for alleles with no table match. `consequence_counts`, `impact_counts` and
`gene_counts` omit zero counts and are sorted by key.

### Get a run

`GET /runs/run-1` returns the run document shown above.

### Get run variants

`GET /runs/run-1/variants` returns `{"count":<n>,"run_id":"run-1","variants":[...]}`
in file order. Each variant repeats the parsed fields plus `raw`, the original
line, so every output stays traceable to the input:

```json
{"alts":["A"],
 "annotations":[{"allele":"A","allele_index":1,"consequence":"missense_variant","gene":"MTHFR","impact":"MODERATE"}],
 "chrom":"chr1","dp":42,"filter":["PASS"],"id":"rs1","info":{"DP":"42"},"line":4,
 "pos":11856378,"qual":60.0,"raw":"chr1\t11856378\trs1\tG\tA\t60\tPASS\tDP=42","ref":"G"}
```

`line` is the 1-based line of the record in the uploaded VCF and `allele_index`
is the 1-based VCF ALT index.

### Export run results

`GET /runs/run-1/exports/jsonl`, `GET /runs/run-1/exports/tsv` and
`GET /runs/run-1/exports/vcf` hand the
retained variants of a saved run to downstream analysis as a stable payload.
The body is generated on demand from the stored run; it is never written to
disk, and the run, its variants and its provenance are not modified.

`jsonl` is served as `application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8`: one variant object
per line in the original file order, using the same fields and values as
`GET /runs/{run_id}/variants`. Each line is UTF-8 JSON with no indentation and
keys sorted lexicographically, terminated by a single LF; the body ends with
the last line's LF (no trailing blank line). A run with no variants returns an
empty body.

`tsv` is served as `text/tab-separated-values; charset=utf-8` and always opens
with the fixed header:

```
chrom	pos	id	ref	alt	allele_index	gene	consequence	impact	qual	dp	filter	info	line
```

Each retained annotation is one row, so a record with several retained ALT
alleles spans several rows; variant file order and annotation order are kept.
Formatting rules:

- `id`, `gene`, `qual` or `dp` is `NA` when null; `qual` otherwise keeps the
  JSON decimal form (e.g. `60.0`);
- an empty `FILTER` is `.`; several filters are joined with `;`;
- `INFO` is `;`-joined `KEY=VALUE` pairs sorted by key; bare flags are written
  as `KEY`; empty INFO is `.`;
- numbers use the JSON decimal representation and text is not quoted.

A run with no variants returns just the header line. An unknown `run_id`
returns 404 `not_found`; any `format` other than `jsonl`, `tsv` or `vcf`
returns 400 `validation_error`, both with the standard error object.

`vcf` is served as `text/x-variant-call-format; charset=utf-8`: the retained
variants rendered back as VCF v4.2 text (UTF-8, LF line endings). The header
opens with `##fileformat=VCFv4.2`, repeats the uploaded sample's other meta
lines in their original order, adds `##source=variantrail`, and declares four
export INFO keys — `ALLELE_INDEX` (Integer), `VT_GENE`, `VT_CONSEQUENCE` and
`VT_IMPACT` (String, all `Number=1`) — before the tab-separated
`#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO` column header. Each retained ALT
allele is one record, in variant file order and `allele_index` order, with
`ALT` holding only the current allele. `ID`, `QUAL` and an empty `FILTER` are
`.` when missing; `INFO` lists the original entries sorted by key, then the
four export keys (`VT_GENE` is `NA` when no gene is annotated). If an original
INFO field uses `ALLELE_INDEX` or one of the `VT_*` keys, the export returns
400 `validation_error` naming the conflicting key. A run with no variants
returns just the header, and repeated requests are byte-identical.

### Compare two runs

`GET /runs/{run_id}/compare/{other_run_id}` compares the retained ALT alleles
of two finished runs — `run_id` on the left, `other_run_id` on the right. It
only reads the stored runs: no pipeline step is re-executed and neither run,
its variants, its exports, nor its provenance is modified. The runs may belong
to different samples. No `Idempotency-Key` is required.

An allele's identity is the tuple `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)`; duplicates of the
same identity within one run count once. Returns HTTP 200:

```json
{"left":{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":8},
 "right":{"run_id":"run-2","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":4},
 "counts":{"shared":4,"left_only":4,"right_only":0,"union":8},
 "shared":[{"chrom":"chr1","pos":11856378,"ref":"G","alt":"T",
   "gene":"MTHFR","consequence":"stop_gained","impact":"HIGH"}],
 "left_only":[...],
 "right_only":[...],
 "gene_summary":{"MTHFR":{"shared":1,"left_only":1,"right_only":0}},
 "impact_summary":{"HIGH":{"shared":4,"left_only":0,"right_only":0}}}
```

- `shared`, `left_only` and `right_only` hold every distinct allele on both
  sides, on the left only, and on the right only; each element carries
  `chrom`, `pos`, `ref`, `alt`, `gene`, `consequence` and `impact`, with
  `gene` kept as JSON `null` when the allele has no table match. Comparing a
  run with itself puts every allele in `shared`.
- Each array is sorted by `chrom` (text order), then `pos` (numeric), then
  `ref`, then `alt`, so repeated requests are byte-for-byte identical.
- `counts` mirrors the three array lengths plus `union`, their total.
- `gene_summary` and `impact_summary` count the alleles of each bucket per
  gene and per impact; keys are sorted lexicographically, a `null` gene
  appears as `NA`, and impacts keep their original values.

An unknown `run_id` or `other_run_id` returns 404 `not_found` with the
message `run <run_id> was not found`.

### Compare a cohort of runs

`GET /runs/{run_id}/cohort/{other_run_ids}` compares the retained ALT alleles
of two or more finished runs at once. `other_run_ids` is two or more run ids
joined with commas; the path order (the path `run_id` first, then the comma
list) is the cohort queue order. Like the two-run comparison it only reads the
stored runs: no pipeline step is re-executed and no run, variant, export or
provenance record is modified. No `Idempotency-Key` is required.

An allele's identity is again `(chrom, pos, ref, alt)`; duplicates of the same
identity within one run count once, and annotations are taken as stored — no
filtering or re-annotation happens. Returns HTTP 200:

```json
{"run_count":3,
 "runs":[{"run_id":"run-1","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":8},
         {"run_id":"run-2","sample_id":"trio-1","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":4},
         {"run_id":"run-3","sample_id":"trio-2","sample_sha256":"...","allele_count":3}],
 "alleles":[{"chrom":"chr1","pos":11856378,"ref":"G","alt":"A","gene":"MTHFR",
   "consequence":"missense_variant","impact":"MODERATE","run_count":2,
   "present_in":["run-1","run-3"]}],
 "counts":{"unique_alleles":9,"core_alleles":2,"variable_alleles":3,
   "private_alleles":{"run-1":3,"run-2":1,"run-3":0}},
 "frequency_summary":{"1":4,"2":3,"3":2},
 "gene_summary":{"BRCA1":{"unique_alleles":1,"core_alleles":1,"variable_alleles":0},
                "MTHFR":{"unique_alleles":2,"core_alleles":0,"variable_alleles":2}},
 "impact_summary":{"HIGH":{"unique_alleles":4,"core_alleles":2,"variable_alleles":2}}}
```

- `runs` repeats the queued runs in queue order; each entry has `run_id`,
  `sample_id`, `sample_sha256` and `allele_count`, the number of distinct
  retained alleles in that run.
- `alleles` holds every distinct allele of the union (different ALTs at the
  same coordinate are separate entries). Each element carries `chrom`, `pos`,
  `ref`, `alt`, `gene` (`null` when the allele has no table match),
  `consequence`, `impact`, `run_count` — the number of cohort runs containing
  it — and `present_in`, the run ids of those runs in queue order. The array
  is sorted by `chrom` (text order), then `pos` (numeric), then `ref`, then
  `alt`, so repeated requests are byte-for-byte identical.
- `counts.unique_alleles` is the total number of entries in `alleles`;
  `core_alleles` counts alleles present in all `run_count` runs,
  `variable_alleles` alleles present in between 2 and `run_count - 1` runs,
  and `private_alleles` breaks the alleles present in exactly one run down by
  `run_id`, in queue order (runs without a private allele show `0`).
- `frequency_summary` has the string keys `"1"` through
  `"<run_count>"` and counts alleles present in exactly that many runs, with
  missing frequencies filled in as `0`.
- `gene_summary` and `impact_summary` group `unique_alleles`, `core_alleles`
  and `variable_alleles` per gene and per impact; a `null` gene appears as
  `NA`, categories with no alleles are omitted, and keys are sorted
  lexicographically. Private alleles are not separately listed there
  (`unique = core + variable + private`).

Changing the queue order returns the same data apart from the order of `runs`
and of each `present_in`; the allele set, counts and summaries are unchanged,
and repeating a request is byte-identical.

Fewer than two run ids in the path is a 400 `validation_error` with the
message `cohort requires at least two distinct runs`; a repeated run id is a
409 `conflict` with the message `cohort run ids must be distinct`; any run id
that does not exist is a 404 `not_found` with the message
`run <run_id> was not found`.

### The annotation table

Annotation matches the exact tuple `(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT)`. A variant with no
matching row is annotated `gene: null`, `consequence: "intergenic_variant"`,
`impact: "MODIFIER"`.

```
chr1  11856378  G  A    MTHFR  missense_variant       MODERATE
chr1  11856378  G  T    MTHFR  stop_gained            HIGH
chr7  55019017  G  GA   EGFR   frameshift_variant     HIGH
chr7  55019017  G  T    EGFR   stop_gained            HIGH
chr7  55273000  C  T    EGFR   synonymous_variant     LOW
chr11 5227002   T  C    HBB    missense_variant       MODERATE
chr12 25245350  C  A    KRAS   missense_variant       MODERATE
chr12 25245350  C  T    KRAS   missense_variant       MODERATE
chr12 25245351  C  T    KRAS   splice_donor_variant   HIGH
chr17 43093445  C  T    BRCA1  stop_gained            HIGH
chr17 43093446  A  G    BRCA1  missense_variant       MODERATE
chr17 7676154   C  T    TP53   missense_variant       MODERATE
chr19 11200138  C  T    LDLR   missense_variant       MODERATE
chrX  31137345  A  G    DMD    missense_variant       MODERATE
```

This is a small synthetic table with GRCh38-style chromosome names and real gene
symbols; the coordinates are illustrative and it is not a clinical annotation
source.

### Get run provenance

`GET /runs/run-1/provenance` returns `{"run_id","verified","chain_verified",
"reproduction_verified","head_sha256","steps":[...]}`, where a step looks like:

```json
{"step":1,"name":"ingest","params":{"parser_version":"variantrail-vcf-1"},
 "input_sha256":"45520c9b2b4798adafe3bdbaf137c567536527581c259dc2d92c391baf2a94ef",
 "output_sha256":"0f5d73dd61762cefc2df233d1e604de50d21df017a6f9e5608851a3c700c6103",
 "previous_sha256":null,
 "hash":"6de42193fc25e82afb9c32b0d6170629b69eb25268d978864f9162b27ed75530"}
```

Write `canonical(x)` for `json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",",":"),
sort_keys=True)` and `H(x)` for the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of the UTF-8
bytes of `canonical(x)`. The four links are:

| step | name | params | input_sha256 | output_sha256 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `ingest` | `{"parser_version":"variantrail-vcf-1"}` | SHA-256 of the VCF text | `H({"records":<parsed records>})` |
| 2 | `filter` | `min_dp`, `min_qual`, `pass_only` | step 1 `output_sha256` | `H({"filter_counts":<3 record keys>,"records":<kept records>})` |
| 3 | `annotate` | `annotation_table_sha256`, `genes`, `impacts` | step 2 `output_sha256` | `H({"filter_counts":<4 keys>,"variants":<variants>})` |
| 4 | `summarize` | `{}` | step 3 `output_sha256` | `H(<statistics>)` |

Each link's own hash covers the previous link, so the trail is tamper-evident:

```
body = {step, name, params, input_sha256, output_sha256, previous_sha256}
hash = H(body)                 # previous_sha256 is null for step 1
```

`chain_verified` recomputes every link hash and checks that each
`previous_sha256` equals the previous link's `hash`. `reproduction_verified`
re-reads the stored sample VCF, re-executes all four steps with the stored
`params`, and compares the four `output_sha256` values, the statistics and the
variants. `verified` is the conjunction of both; the endpoint never rewrites the
stored trail.

## Errors

```json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"line 5: POS must be a positive integer"}}
```

Validation errors return 400, missing resources 404, conflicts 409. A missing
`Idempotency-Key` header is a `validation_error`, and reusing one key for a
different operation is a `conflict`.

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Now I understand the codebase. Let me plan the implementation of `record_filter`:

**Requirements summary:**

1. `params.record_filter` — optional structured JSON expression for record-level combination conditions.
2. When absent: only the original five params are stored; statistics, variant order, and four-step provenance hashes unchanged.
3. When present: run details and filter step save the normalized full expression; same sample + params → same results and hashes.
4. Expression nodes: exactly one of `all`, `any`, `not`, or a condition object.
   - `all`/`any`: non-empty arrays of sub-expressions.
   - `not`: single sub-expression.
   - Condition object: `field`, `op`, and `value` as needed by op.
   - Fields: `chrom`, `pos`, `id`, `ref`, `alt`, `qual`, `dp`, `filter`, `info.<KEY>`.
   - Ops: `eq`, `in`, `lt`, `lte`, `gt`, `gte`, `exists`.
   - `eq`: direct scalar comparison; `in`: value must be non-empty array, membership test. For `alt` and `filter` fields, both eq and in are true if any element matches.
   - Size comparisons (lt/lte/gt/gte): require numeric value; only apply to `pos`, `qual`, `dp`, or INFO values fully parseable as finite decimal numbers.

class RecordFilterTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.service = VariantRail(str(Path(self.directory.name) / "test.db"))

    def tearDown(self):
        self.directory.cleanup()

    def sample(self, key="s1", vcf=VCF, sample_id="s1"):
        return self.service.create_sample({"id": sample_id, "vcf": vcf}, key)

    def start_run(self, params=None, key="r1", run_id="run-1", sample_id="s1"):
        body = {"id": run_id}
        if params is not None:
            body["params"] = params
        return self.service.create_run(sample_id, body, key)

    def kept_lines(self, run_id="run-1"):
        return [variant["line"] for variant in self.service.run_variants(run_id)["variants"]]

    def test_eq_on_a_scalar_field(self):
        self.sample()
        run = self.start_run({"record_filter": {"field": "chrom", "op": "eq", "value": "chr7"}})
        self.assertEqual([8, 9], self.kept_lines())
        self.assertEqual(
            {"allele_filtered": 0, "dp_below_min": 0, "not_pass": 0, "qual_below_min": 0, "rule_mismatch": 5},
            run["statistics"]["filter_counts"],
        )
        self.assertEqual(5, run["statistics"]["records_filtered"])
        self.assertEqual(2, run["statistics"]["records_kept"])

    def test_in_and_any_element_semantics_for_alt_and_filter(self):
        self.sample()
        run = self.start_run({"record_filter": {"field": "alt", "op": "in", "value": ["GA", "T"]}})
        self.assertEqual([6, 8, 9, 10, 11], self.kept_lines())
        self.assertEqual(2, run["statistics"]["filter_counts"]["rule_mismatch"])
        run = self.start_run(
            {"record_filter": {"field": "filter", "op": "eq", "value": "q10"}}, key="r2", run_id="run-2"
        )
        self.assertEqual([7], self.kept_lines("run-2"))
        run = self.start_run(
            {"record_filter": {"field": "filter", "op": "eq", "value": "PASS"}}, key="r3", run_id="run-3"
        )
        self.assertEqual([5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11], self.kept_lines("run-3"))

    def test_exists_and_null_semantics(self):
        self.sample()
        run = self.start_run({"record_filter": {"field": "qual", "op": "exists"}})
        self.assertEqual([5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11], self.kept_lines())
        run = self.start_run({"record_filter": {"field": "id", "op": "exists"}}, key="r2", run_id="run-2")
        self.assertEqual([5, 6], self.kept_lines("run-2"))
        # A null qual fails eq and comparisons but can be inverted with not.
        run = self.start_run(
            {"record_filter": {"not": {"field": "qual", "op": "exists"}}}, key="r3", run_id="run-3"
        )
        self.assertEqual([7], self.kept_lines("run-3"))

    def test_comparisons_on_pos_qual_dp_and_info(self):
        self.sample()
        run = self.start_run({"record_filter": {"field": "pos", "op": "gte", "value": 55019017}})
        self.assertEqual([8, 9, 10, 11], self.kept_lines())
        run = self.start_run({"record_filter": {"field": "qual", "op": "lt", "value": 60}}, key="r2", run_id="run-2")
        self.assertEqual([6, 8, 9], self.kept_lines("run-2"))
        run = self.start_run({"record_filter": {"field": "dp", "op": "gt", "value": 42}}, key="r3", run_id="run-3")
        self.assertEqual([10, 11], self.kept_lines("run-3"))
        # INFO/DP is a string in storage; numeric ops parse it, missing DP is false.
        run = self.start_run(
            {"record_filter": {"field": "info.DP", "op": "lte", "value": 42}}, key="r4", run_id="run-4"
        )
        self.assertEqual([5, 6, 7, 8], self.kept_lines("run-4"))

    def test_info_flags_eq_and_unparseable_numbers(self):
        vcf = "\n".join(
            [
                PREAMBLE,
                HEADER,
                "chr1\t100\t.\tA\tG\t10\tPASS\tDP=30;AF=0.25;FLAG",
                "chr1\t200\t.\tA\tG\t20\tPASS\tDP=5;AF=high",
                "chr1\t300\t.\tA\tG\t.\tq10\t.",
            ]
        ) + "\n"
        self.sample(vcf=vcf)
        # A bare INFO flag counts as existing.
        run = self.start_run({"record_filter": {"field": "info.FLAG", "op": "exists"}})
        self.assertEqual([5], self.kept_lines())
        # ...but its null value fails eq like any other missing value.
        run = self.start_run(
            {"record_filter": {"field": "info.FLAG", "op": "eq", "value": "FLAG"}}, key="r2", run_id="run-2"
        )
        self.assertEqual([], self.kept_lines("run-2"))
        # eq compares the stored INFO string verbatim.
        run = self.start_run(
            {"record_filter": {"field": "info.AF", "op": "eq", "value": "0.25"}}, key="r3", run_id="run-3"
        )
        self.assertEqual([5], self.kept_lines("r3".replace("r3", "run-3")))

        body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}{path}",
            data=body,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Idempotency-Key": key},
            method="POST",
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
                return response.status, response.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            body = error.read()
            status = error.code
            error.close()
            return status, body
